title: Cain to the Flood, part 3 of 5: the flood comes
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of Noah and the great flood: people dressed in simple garments of rough undyed wool or animal skin, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

NOAH.name: Noah
NOAH.desc: Noah, a strong weathered man who looks about fifty, with warm brown skin, thick grey-streaked dark hair to his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, deep-set kind eyes and a lined brow, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed brown wool with a leather belt and a darker wool mantle over one shoulder, and simple leather sandals

NOAH_WIFE.name: Noah's wife
NOAH_WIFE.desc: Noah's wife, a strong, kind-faced woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, grey-streaked black hair in one long thick braid over her shoulder, dark warm eyes and laughter lines, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough undyed cream wool with a brown wool shawl around her shoulders, and simple leather sandals

SHEM.name: Shem
SHEM.desc: Shem, a son of Noah, a lean, thoughtful man of about thirty with warm brown skin, wavy black hair to his jaw and a short neat black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed cream wool with a rope belt, and simple leather sandals

HAM.name: Ham
HAM.desc: Ham, a son of Noah, a stocky, broad-shouldered man of about thirty with warm brown skin, close-cropped curly black hair and a thick short black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough rust-brown wool with a leather belt, and simple leather sandals

JAPHETH.name: Japheth
JAPHETH.desc: Japheth, a son of Noah, a tall, rangy man of about thirty with warm brown skin, long straight black hair tied back at the nape of his neck and a thin beard along his jaw, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough dark-grey wool with a leather belt, and simple leather sandals

blocks.TWO: Exactly two people in the picture, one man and one woman, no one else
blocks.NOLIGHTFIG: No figure, no face and no human shape in the light
blocks.TOWN: a town of the world before the flood: crowded low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and rough stone and dark goat-hair tents, with no towers, no arches, no temples, no statues and no carved decoration
blocks.CLOUDS: a heavy bank of dark grey cloud massing across the sky, with no rain falling and no lightning
blocks.ARK: the ark: an enormous, very long rectangular vessel like a great chest, built of dark timber coated black with pitch, with straight vertical sides, squared ends and a flat bottom resting on the ground, ten times as long as it is high, with a low-pitched plank roof, a narrow open gap running the whole length just under the eaves, and one large door in the middle of its long side; no mast, no sail, no oars, no rudder, no pointed prow, no curved hull and no windows in its sides
blocks.WIFE_S: Shem's wife, a slim woman in her twenties with warm brown skin and long black hair in two braids, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough undyed cream wool
blocks.WIFE_H: Ham's wife, a sturdy woman in her twenties with warm brown skin and curly black hair bound up in a rust-brown wool headcloth, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough rust-brown wool
blocks.WIFE_J: Japheth's wife, a tall woman in her twenties with warm brown skin and straight black hair in one long plait down her back, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough dark-grey wool
blocks.TWO_MEN: Exactly two people in the picture, both men, no one else
blocks.ARKFLOAT: the ark afloat: an enormous, very long rectangular vessel like a great chest, built of dark timber coated black with pitch, with straight vertical sides and squared ends, riding low and level in the water, ten times as long as it is high, with a low-pitched plank roof, a narrow open gap running the whole length just under the eaves, and one large door, shut tight, in the middle of its long side; no mast, no sail, no oars, no rudder, no pointed prow, no curved hull, no windows in its sides and no one on its roof
blocks.ARKWALL: the towering straight black pitch-coated timber wall of the ark, with a broad timber ramp leading up to the one large open door in the middle of its long side
blocks.INSIDE: inside the ark: a long low deck of heavy dark timber with stout posts and beams and rows of wooden stalls and pens strewn with straw, lit by small clay oil lamps, with no windows
blocks.RAIN: heavy rain falling in grey slanting sheets from a black sky
blocks.NOLAND: No land, no shore, no trees and no rocks anywhere, only water to every horizon
blocks.NODEAD: No bodies, no people and no animals anywhere in the picture
blocks.CALM: The animals are calm and unafraid, and none is led, roped or driven
blocks.FLATWALL: a towering, perfectly flat, straight vertical wall of horizontal timber planks coated black with pitch, like the side of an enormous barn, not curved anywhere and not shaped like the hull of a ship

segs.text: Then the LORD said to Noah,
Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female, to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.
For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made.
And Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him.
Now Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
And Noah and his wife, with his sons and their wives, entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.
The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground
came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah entered the ark, along with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and his wife, and the three wives of his sons—
they and every kind of wild animal, livestock, crawling creature, bird, and winged creature.
They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two of every creature with the breath of life.
And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.
So the waters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.
Finally, the waters completely prevailed upon the earth, so that all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.
The waters rose and covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.
And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished—birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

And every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed—man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.

stills.prompt: Then the LORD said to Noah: {NOAH}, standing alone on a level plain with his face lifted, while from the sky {GLORY}, falls across him; far behind him stands the long black shape of the finished ark. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NORAIN}. Wide view.

Go into the ark, you and all your family: eight people standing in a row at the foot of a broad timber ramp, seen from the front, with {FLATWALL}, rising behind them and a large open doorway at the top of the ramp. In the middle stand {NOAH}, and {NOAH_WIFE}. On their left stand two young couples and on their right one young couple: three bearded men of about thirty in knee-length wool tunics, one cream, one rust-brown and one dark grey, each with his young wife beside him in a long wool dress of the same colour as his tunic. Exactly eight adults: four men and four women, standing as four couples; no children, no one else. Grave, quiet faces. {NORAIN}. Wide view.

I have found you righteous in this generation: {NOAH}, kneeling on the bare ground with his head bowed and his open hands resting on his knees, a warm shaft of golden light falling on him alone while the land around him lies in cloud shadow. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium close view.

Every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate: a horned ram and a ewe standing close side by side on a grassy slope in the foreground, the ram's curled horns plain to see, and behind them more sheep following in a column two abreast that runs out of the picture. {NOPEOPLE}. {NORAIN}. Medium view.

Seven pairs: seen from directly above, fourteen sheep walking along a dusty path in a neat column two abreast, seven rows of two, each row a horned ram beside a ewe. Exactly fourteen sheep in seven pairs, no more and no fewer. {NOPEOPLE}. High overhead view.

A pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate: two camels, a large bull camel and a smaller cow camel, walking alone side by side across a stony plain under a heavy sky, with no other animals near them. Exactly two camels, no riders, no saddles, no ropes. {NOPEOPLE}. {NORAIN}. Wide view.

Every kind of bird of the air, male and female: a flight of white and grey doves coming down in pairs out of a heavy sky to settle along the long plank roof of the ark, whose black pitch-coated wall fills the lower part of the picture. {NOPEOPLE}. {NORAIN}. Low-angle medium-wide view.

To preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth: a close view of a nest of twigs in the fork of an olive tree holding four small pale eggs, with two grey doves perched together on the branch beside it. Exactly two birds. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view.
Seven days from now I will send rain on the earth: {NOAH}, standing on dry cracked ground and looking up at the sky, where {CLOUDS}, hangs over a still, dry land. {ONE}. Low-angle medium view.

Every living thing I have made: a wide green river valley seen from a hillside, full of life, with herds of deer and wild cattle grazing, flocks of birds wheeling over the water, and the smoke of a far village rising, all lying under a darkening sky. {NORAIN}. Very wide view.

Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him: {NOAH}, walking up a broad timber ramp with a heavy sack of grain on his shoulder, toward a large open doorway in {FLATWALL}, which fills the whole background. {ONE}. {NORAIN}. Medium-wide low-angle view.

Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came: a close portrait of {NOAH}, his weathered face turned toward the horizon, the wind lifting his grey-streaked hair, a black wall of cloud reflected dimly in his eyes. {ONE}. {NORAIN}. Close view, head and shoulders.

Noah and his wife entered the ark: {NOAH}, and {NOAH_WIFE}, seen from behind and a little to one side, walking away from us side by side up a broad timber ramp and about to step into a large dark open doorway in {FLATWALL}; she looks back over her shoulder with a grave face. {TWO}. {NORAIN}. No water on the ground. Medium-wide view.

With his sons and their wives: three couples seen from behind and a little to one side, walking away from us up a broad timber ramp toward a large dark open doorway in {FLATWALL}, carrying bundles and clay jars, some glancing back over their shoulders with grave faces: {SHEM}, with {WIFE_S}; {HAM}, with {WIFE_H}; and {JAPHETH}, with {WIFE_J}. Exactly six people: three men and three women, no children, no one else. {NORAIN}. Medium-wide view.

To escape the waters of the flood: the view outward from inside the dark doorway of the ark, the heavy timber door frame black around the edges of the picture, looking down a timber ramp and out over a wide plain where {CLOUDS}, presses low over the land. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view from inside looking out.

The clean and unclean animals: a long procession of animals in pairs crossing an open plain toward the distant long black shape of the ark: two oxen, two sheep, two goats, two camels, two donkeys and two deer, each pair walking side by side. {CALM}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NORAIN}. Wide view.

The birds: pairs of birds flying together across a heavy grey sky: two storks, two ravens, two eagles and two doves, each pair wing to wing, all gliding down toward the long black roof of the ark, which stands far below them on a dry grassy plain. No sea and no water anywhere. {NOPEOPLE}. {NORAIN}. Wide view from the air.

Everything that crawls along the ground: seen close and low, two tortoises, two green lizards and two beetles crawling up the rough planks of a timber ramp, all heading the same way. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view, low to the planks.

They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two: {NOAH}, standing at the top of a broad timber ramp beside a large open doorway in {FLATWALL}, which fills the whole background, watching as pairs of animals walk up the ramp toward him of their own accord: two deer, two goats and two wolves. {CALM}. {ONE}. {NORAIN}. Medium-wide view.

Male and female: a maned lion and a lioness walking side by side through the large open timber doorway of the ark, out of grey daylight into the lamplit dark. Exactly two animals: one male lion with a mane and one lioness. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium view.
As God had commanded Noah: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, closes the wooden gate of a straw-filled stall on a ram and a ewe. Exactly one person and two sheep. Medium view.

And after seven days: the finished ark standing on the plain under a black and lowering sky, seen from the side, its one large door standing open with a faint glow of lamplight inside and the timber ramp empty; wind flattens the grass. It is {ARK}. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

The floodwaters came upon the earth: a close view of the first heavy drops of rain striking dry cracked earth, each drop raising a small burst of dust, dark wet spots spreading. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view of the ground.

In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month: a grey dawn over a wide plain, the whole sky a ceiling of black churning cloud with a single band of pale light along the horizon, and the long black shape of the ark small in the distance. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.

All the fountains of the great deep burst forth: the ground of a wide plain splitting open in long cracks, and huge white columns of water bursting upward out of the earth high into the air, flinging up rocks and soil. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

The fountains of the great deep: a dark sea heaving as vast domes and towers of white water burst up from beneath its surface and great waves roll outward toward a low coast. {NOPEOPLE}. No ships. Very wide view.

The floodgates of the heavens were opened: seen from the ground looking up, the black clouds torn apart, and water pouring down through the openings in immense solid cataracts, like waterfalls dropping out of the sky. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Low-angle very wide view.
The rain fell upon the earth: {RAIN}, on a river valley, the river brown and swollen and spilling over its banks into the fields, trees bending in the wind. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

Forty days and forty nights: night, a forest standing in rising black water under pouring rain, the trunks and the streaming rain lit for an instant by a white flash of lightning inside the clouds. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

On that very day Noah entered the ark: {NOAH}, striding up a wet timber ramp in the first driving rain toward a large open doorway in {FLATWALL}, his mantle pulled over his head and his face turned back over his shoulder toward the storm. The ramp stands on muddy ground with puddles. No sea, no waves and no flood water yet. {ONE}. Medium-wide view.

Along with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth: three brothers standing together in the rain just outside the large open timber doorway of the ark, lamplight behind them: {SHEM}; {HAM}; and {JAPHETH}. Exactly three people, all men, no one else. Medium view.

And his wife, and the three wives of his sons: four women hurrying up a wet timber ramp in the rain toward a large open doorway in {FLATWALL}, their shawls drawn over their heads and their faces grave: {NOAH_WIFE}, leading, and behind her {WIFE_S}, and {WIFE_H}, and {WIFE_J}. The ramp stands on muddy ground with puddles. No sea, no waves and no flood water yet. Exactly four women, no men, no one else. Medium-wide view.

Every kind of wild animal and livestock: two grey wolves and two brown cattle, a bull and a cow, walking up a wet timber ramp in the rain, the wolves beside the cattle and neither heeding the other. Exactly four animals: two wolves and two cattle. {CALM}. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium view.

Crawling creature, bird and winged creature: two owls and two small bats flying in through the top of the large open timber doorway of the ark out of the rain, while two lizards climb the wet door post below them. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium view looking up at the doorway.

They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two: seen from inside a dark timber room, looking out through a large open doorway: {NOAH}, stands in the doorway, seen from behind as a dark shape against the grey rain; beyond him a timber ramp slopes down to a muddy plain, and a long line of animals in pairs, two oxen, two deer and two goats, walks up the ramp toward him out of the storm. Outside there is no boat, no ship, no building and no sea. {CALM}. {ONE}. Wide view from inside.

Every creature with the breath of life: a close view of the heads of two horses, a stallion and a mare, side by side in cold rain, their breath steaming white from their nostrils. Exactly two horses, no bridles, no ropes. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view.

The male and female of every living thing: {INSIDE}, with pairs of animals settled in the stalls on both sides, two oxen, two deer, two goats and two donkeys, and pairs of doves roosting on the beams above. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide interior view down the length of the deck.
As God had commanded Noah: {NOAH}, standing just inside the large open doorway of the ark, one hand on the heavy timber door frame, looking out into {RAIN}. {ONE}. Medium view from inside.

Then the LORD shut him in: {FLATWALL}, seen from outside in the rain and filling the picture, its one large timber door shut tight, the timber ramp before it empty, and falling on the closed door alone {GLORY}. The door is completely closed. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. No hand on the door. Medium-wide low-angle view.

The LORD shut him in: in the darkness inside the ark, {NOAH}, seen from behind and to one side, standing before the great timber door, which is shut tight, with a thin line of golden light glowing all around its edges, his open hand resting flat against the wood. {ONE}. Medium view.

For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth: {RAIN}, on a plain that has become a wide brown lake, and standing in the shallow rising water the ark, still resting on the ground, its door shut: {ARK}. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

The waters rose and lifted the ark: in pouring rain, brown floodwater swirling and foaming along the foot of {FLATWALL}, the long side of the ark, as it comes free of the ground and begins to float, loose timbers of the ramp and scaffolding washing away beside it. Its one door is shut. No prow, no bow, no keel and no rudder. {NOPEOPLE}. Low medium-wide view at the waterline, looking along the wall.

High above the earth: seen from high above in the rain, {ARKFLOAT}, drifting over drowned country, with the tops of tall trees and the crest of one low hill still showing above the brown water far around it. {NOPEOPLE}. High wide view.

The waters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth: a wild brown torrent tearing down a rocky valley in the rain, carrying uprooted trees and breaking in white surges against the cliffs. {NODEAD}. Wide view.
The ark floated on the surface of the waters: {ARKFLOAT}, seen whole from the side on a heaving grey sea under {RAIN}. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.

Inside the floating ark: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, and {NOAH_WIFE}, sit close together on a timber bench by the light of one clay oil lamp that hangs swinging from a beam, listening to the storm outside. {TWO}. Medium view.

The waters completely prevailed upon the earth: grey water climbing the flanks of green hills until only their rounded tops stand out like islands in a wide sea, in steady rain. {NODEAD}. No boats. Very wide view.

All the high mountains under all the heavens were covered: a range of great snow-covered mountains with the sea risen almost to their summits, only the last jagged peaks standing above grey waves that break against the rock and snow, under a black sky. {NODEAD}. No boats. Very wide view.

The waters rose and covered the mountaintops: the very last bare rocky summit of a mountain, a small point of wet stone alone in an endless grey sea, with a wave rising to close over it. {NODEAD}. No boats. Medium-wide view.

To a depth of fifteen cubits: an underwater view in dim green light, looking across the submerged rocky summit of a mountain; above it lies a clear band of water, and above that, at the surface, the long flat dark underside of the ark passes over without touching the rock. {NODEAD}. No fish. Wide underwater view.

Every living thing that moved upon the earth perished, birds: a few weary birds flying low over an endless grey sea in the rain, searching, with nowhere to land. {NOLAND}. No boats. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

Livestock and animals: an underwater view in dim green light of a drowned pasture, a round drystone sheepfold with its wooden gate hanging open and empty, and a shepherd's wooden crook drifting slowly down through the water. {NODEAD}. No fish. Wide underwater view.

And all mankind: an underwater view in dim green light of a drowned street in {TOWN}, the doorways dark and empty, a clay jar and a wooden stool drifting in the water above the street. {NODEAD}. No fish. Wide underwater view.

Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died: on rolling grey water under rain, an uprooted tree, a broken wooden sledge of lashed poles and an empty woven reed basket drift together. {NOLAND}. {NODEAD}. No boats. Medium-wide view.

Every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed: an underwater view in dim green light of a drowned field, a wooden plough and an ox yoke lying abandoned in a furrow and a cold ring of hearth stones beside a fallen goat-hair tent. {NODEAD}. No fish. Wide underwater view.

They were blotted out from the earth: seen from very high above, an unbroken dark ocean under torn grey clouds, stretching to a curved horizon. {NOLAND}. No boats and no ark. {NODEAD}. Very high, very wide view.

Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained: a vast empty grey sea under a heavy sky, and alone on it, very small in the distance, {ARKFLOAT}, with a faint warm glow of lamplight showing along the gap under its eaves. {NOLAND}. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.

Noah and those with him in the ark: {INSIDE}, where eight people sit close together in a circle on the straw around one clay oil lamp, with grave, quiet faces. Facing us sit {NOAH}, and beside him {NOAH_WIFE}. Completing the circle are three young couples: three bearded men of about thirty in wool tunics, one cream, one rust-brown and one dark grey, each with his young wife beside him in a long wool dress of the same colour as his tunic; some are seen from behind. Exactly eight adults: four men and four women; no children, no one else. Wide view.
The waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days: a calm, still, silver-grey sea under a pale veiled sun, the rain ended, and far off {ARKFLOAT}, drifting. {NOLAND}. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.

150 days: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, cuts one more short straight notch with a bronze knife into a timber post already marked with neat rows of short plain straight notches like tally marks, with no letters, no symbols and no pictures. No window and no daylight. {ONE}. Medium close view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 7:1–24, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 7:1-24 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (7:1-4). Noah does not speak in this chapter. Every used verse was read for typos in the snapshot: none found.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces and designs reused word for word from s01e02b: NOAH, NOAH_WIFE, SHEM, HAM, JAPHETH (sheets refs/REF-NOAH.jpg and the four made by s01e02b), blocks ARK, WIFE_S, WIFE_H, WIFE_J, GLORY, TOWN, CLOUDS. Noah stays the weathered man of about fifty although 7:6 gives his age as 600 (I, as decided in s01e02b).

New blocks for Genesis 8-9 to reuse word for word: ARKFLOAT (the ARK text with 'resting on the ground' replaced by 'riding low and level in the water' and the door shut), INSIDE (the lamplit stall deck), ARKWALL, RAIN, NOLAND, NODEAD. The ark still has no window in these pictures; Genesis 8:6 mentions a window Noah had made, which the unit for Genesis 8 must place (for example a hatch in the roof or in the gap under the eaves) without changing the sides.

The chapter tells the entry into the ark twice (7:7-9 and again 7:13-16, 'on that very day'). The pictures follow the text's order and do not harmonise: under 7:7-9 the family and the animals go in beneath heavy cloud with no rain; 7:10 shows the first drops; 7:11-12 the fountains and the rain; under 7:13-16 the same entry is seen in the first driving rain of that day, and the door is shut. How the seven days of 7:4 and 7:10 relate to the loading is left open.

Clean and unclean (7:2, 7:8): the text does not say here which animals are which. Sheep, cattle, goats and deer stand for the clean and camels and donkeys for the unclean, following Leviticus 11 (I). 'Seven pairs' follows the BSB main text; B2 tries to show fourteen sheep in seven pairs and must be counted at review; elsewhere the columns of clean animals run out of the frame so no number is asserted. The unclean pair (B3) is exactly two.

The animals come of their own accord (7:9, 7:15 'came to Noah'): none is led, roped or driven (block CALM). Predators walk beside livestock without harm (N1), which is I from the text's 'two by two of every creature'.

God is light only (GLORY). 'The LORD shut him in' (7:16): the door is seen shut with the light resting on it (P3) and from inside with light around its edges (P4); no hand, no figure and no person closes it, and the moment of closing is not shown.

'The fountains of the great deep' and 'the floodgates of the heavens' (7:11): painted as the words say, water bursting up from the ground and the sea and falling through torn cloud, with no theory of the mechanism. Lightning (L2) is D.

'Fifteen cubits' (7:20): T2 shows the ark passing clear above a drowned summit. That the depth relates to the ark's draught is an old inference (I); the picture only shows clear water over the mountaintop. Whether the flood was worldwide or regional is not argued: the pictures show what the words say (all the high mountains covered, no land to any horizon).

Death (7:21-23): no bodies of people or animals are shown anywhere (block NODEAD). The perishing is told by weary birds with nowhere to land, an empty sheepfold, a drowned street and field, and drifting things. No fish are painted in the underwater views (the text speaks only of what was on dry land).

7:24: the rain has ended in X1 (forty days of rain within the 150). X2, Noah keeping count with notches, is D; R3 and W4, the family by lamplight, are D for the setting and T for who remained (the eight of 7:13).
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
